summary: Frontend-only validation of the focus-trap fix for Payment Details modal in FixedExpenses.js and VariableExpenses.js, plus verification of the 'latest month with data' default for Fixed Expenses. All 5 requested scenarios executed against the preview URL as admin@freshflow.com. Focus-trap fix works correctly in BOTH pages: the Add Dialog closes (Radix dialog count -> 0) before the Payment Details modal opens, the Confirm Payment button is clickable without force (no overlay intercept), and the Cancel button correctly re-opens the Add/Edit dialog so the user can continue editing. However, in VariableExpenses.js, the modal is unreachable in the normal 'Add new expense' flow because formData.payment_date is preset to today's date (line 79), so the trigger condition (formData.payment_status === 'paid' && !formData.payment_date) at handleSubmit line 266 is never satisfied. The modal only opens when editing a pending expense whose stored payment_date is null. This is a latent trigger-logic bug that hides the (now-fixed) focus-trap flow from normal users.

ui_bugs.issue: Payment Details modal never opens on Add flow because formData.payment_date is initialized to today (line 79). Condition `payment_status === 'paid' && !formData.payment_date` is always false for new expenses. Also fails when editing legacy pending records that were created via the same form (they carry a payment_date). Consider (a) initializing payment_date to '' when payment_status === 'pending', OR (b) triggering the modal whenever payment_status is set to 'paid' regardless of payment_date, OR (c) clearing payment_date when user toggles status from pending -> paid.

Not a bug per se, but preview DB has no fixed expenses so the 'latest month with data' logic silently falls back to current month (Aug 2026). Fallback path was NOT exercised with real data. Recommend seeding a fixed expense in a prior month to validate the primary code path.

action_items: HIGH: Fix the VariableExpenses.js trigger for the Payment Details modal. Currently unreachable in the 'Add' flow because payment_date defaults to today. Suggested fix: change line 79 to `payment_date: ''`, mirroring FixedExpenses.js which uses `payment_date: ''` (line 190). Also verify that resetForm/handleEdit clear payment_date consistently.

LOW: Seed at least one Fixed Expense in a prior month (e.g., July 2026) in the preview DB to allow future testing agents to validate the 'latest month with data' primary code path in FixedExpenses.js (lines 103-146).
critical_code_review_comments: VariableExpenses.js line 79: `payment_date: new Date().toISOString().split('T')[0]` preloads today, making the paid-modal trigger dead code for the add flow. This asymmetry with FixedExpenses.js (which uses `payment_date: ''`) is likely unintentional.

FixedExpenses.js latest-month useEffect (lines 103-147) fetches with `?limit=100` but the endpoint's default filter is current month/year (per iter 48 report). If the current month has data, latest-month resolution is effectively current-month. Consider passing an explicit wide date range (or a dedicated endpoint) to reliably discover the latest month across history.

Payment Details modal is implemented as a plain div overlay (z-50) instead of a Radix Dialog. That's fine and actually the reason the focus-trap issue was solved, but consider extracting it into a reusable component - it's duplicated between FixedExpenses.js (lines 926-1035) and VariableExpenses.js (lines 1760+).
Both files are very large (Fixed=1040 lines, Variable=2659 lines). VariableExpenses.js in particular should be split into smaller modules (form, table, filters, payment modal, reimbursement flows).

rca of the issue: Original focus-trap bug: Payment Details modal (a plain div with z-50) was rendered as a sibling of the still-open Radix Dialog (Add Expense). Radix Dialog installs a focus-trap on its content, so buttons inside the sibling overlay could not receive focus/pointer events reliably. Fix (verified working): call setShowAddDialog(false) BEFORE setShowPaymentDetailsModal(true) in handleSubmit, and in the payment modal's Cancel handler, call setShowAddDialog(true) again to preserve the user's edits. Reproduction (after the fix): impossible in Fixed Expenses (fix works). In Variable Expenses, the Add flow does not reach the trigger at all due to the pre-populated payment_date; must edit a pending expense with null payment_date to reach the modal path.
